examples.en: My friend puts the chair back in its original place.
I turned the clock back by an hour.
Shall I turn this desk toward the window?
Please don't turn the fan toward me.
Please be sure to put the borrowed books back in their place.

examples.ko: 아이가 거꾸로 앉은 인형을 바로 돌려놓았어요.
examples.en: The child turned the upside-down doll the right way up.

explain: '돌려주다'는 빌린 것을 남에게 주는 거고, '돌려놓다'는 방향을 바꾸거나 있던 자리에 도로 두는 거예요. 말할 때는 '돌려놔요', '돌려놨어요'처럼 줄여서 많이 써요. '제자리에 돌려놓다'처럼 장소 말과 함께 써요.
explain_en: '돌려주다' means giving something back to someone, while '돌려놓다' means changing the direction of something or putting it back where it was. In speech it is often shortened to '돌려놔요' or '돌려놨어요'. It is used with place words, as in '제자리에 돌려놓다'.

examples.en: The baby's cheeks are so round and cute.
I picked up some round pebbles by the river.
Mom shaped the rice balls into little rounds for me.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 얼굴이 동글동글하고 눈도 커요.
examples.en: That friend has a round face and big eyes.

examples.ko: 이 아이의 동글동글한 글씨가 참 예뻐요.
examples.en: This child's rounded handwriting is really pretty.
After using the soap for a long time, it has become rounded.

explain: '둥글둥글하다'보다 작고 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이에요. 아기 볼, 구슬, 작은 돌처럼 작은 것에 잘 어울려요. 활용은 '동글동글해요', '동글동글한'처럼 해요.
explain_en: It feels smaller, lighter and cuter than '둥글둥글하다'. It suits small things like a baby's cheeks, beads or little stones. It conjugates as '동글동글해요' and '동글동글한'.

examples.ko: 서울에서 동북쪽으로 한 시간쯤 가면 공원이 나와요.
examples.en: If you go northeast from Seoul for about an hour, you reach a park.
The typhoon is slowly moving toward the northeast.
Our school is northeast of City Hall.
Morning sunlight comes in through the northeast window.
According to the compass, that mountain is to the northeast.
The sky in the northeast is full of clouds.

explain: 일상에서는 '동북쪽'과 '북동쪽'을 둘 다 써요. 가는 방향은 '동북쪽으로', 있는 위치는 '동북쪽에'로 말해요. 반대 방향은 '서남쪽'이에요.
explain_en: In daily life both '동북쪽' and '북동쪽' are used. Use '동북쪽으로' for the direction you go and '동북쪽에' for where something is. The opposite direction is '서남쪽'.

examples.en: Today I met a high school classmate after a long time.
Yesterday I went to a university classmate's wedding.
For the first time in a while, former classmates got together for dinner.
I ran into an elementary school classmate on the street.
That person is my middle school classmate.

examples.ko: 이번 주 동창생 모임에 같이 가실래요?
examples.en: Would you like to come to the alumni gathering this week?

explain: 같은 학교를 다닌 사이를 말하고, 줄여서 '동창'이라고도 많이 해요. '고등학교 동창생'처럼 학교 이름을 앞에 붙여서 써요. 같은 해에 입학하거나 입사한 사람은 '동기'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to people who went to the same school, and it is often shortened to '동창'. You usually put the school level in front, as in '고등학교 동창생'. People who entered a school or company in the same year are '동기', which is different.

examples.en: A light east wind is blowing today.

examples.ko: 동풍이 부는 날에는 창문을 닫아 두세요.
examples.en: On days when the east wind blows, please keep the windows closed.
The weather forecast said an east wind will blow tomorrow.
The ship left late because of the east wind.
The flag is shaking hard in the east wind.
This morning the east wind blew pleasantly cool.

explain: 바람 이름은 부는 쪽이 아니라 불어오는 쪽을 따라요. 그래서 동풍은 동쪽에서 오는 바람이에요. 짝말은 '서풍', '남풍', '북풍'이고 '바람이 불다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: Wind names follow the direction the wind comes from, not where it blows to, so an east wind comes from the east. Its counterparts are '서풍', '남풍' and '북풍', and it goes with '바람이 불다'.

examples.en: I borrowed a book of fairy tales from the library.
I bought a fairy tale collection to read to my child.

examples.ko: 이 동화집에는 옛이야기가 열 편 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This collection has ten old tales in it.

examples.ko: 생일 선물로 그림이 예쁜 동화집을 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a fairy tale book with pretty pictures as a birthday present.

examples.ko: 동화집을 침대 옆에 두고 매일 읽어요.
examples.en: I keep the fairy tale book by my bed and read it every day.

examples.ko: 이 작가가 쓴 동화집이 새로 나왔어요.
examples.en: A new fairy tale collection by this author has come out.

explain: '-집'은 글을 모은 책에 붙어요. 시를 모으면 '시집', 소설을 모으면 '소설집'이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '동화책'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-집' attaches to books that gather writings, like '시집' (poems) and '소설집' (stories). In everyday talk people also just say '동화책'.

examples.en: I resold the item I bought cheaply at a higher price.

examples.ko: 쓰던 휴대폰을 중고 가게에 되팔 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to sell my old phone back to a used shop.

examples.ko: 표를 비싸게 되파는 사람들이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: People who resell tickets at high prices were on the news.

examples.ko: 산 지 한 달 된 가방을 되팔고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to resell a bag I bought a month ago.

examples.ko: 책을 읽은 뒤에 중고 서점에 되팔아요.
examples.en: After reading books, I sell them to a used bookstore.

examples.ko: 이 집은 값이 오르면 되팔 생각이에요.
examples.en: I plan to resell this house if the price goes up.

explain: '되-'는 '다시'라는 느낌을 더해요. '되찾다', '되돌리다'와 같은 짝이에요. 'ㄹ' 받침이 있어서 '되파는', '되팝니다'처럼 'ㄹ'이 빠져요.
explain_en: The prefix '되-' adds a sense of 'again' or 'back', like in '되찾다' and '되돌리다'. Since the stem ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops before some endings, as in '되파는' and '되팝니다'.

examples.en: A few people arrived at the meeting room first.
Please just buy two or three apples.
I called a few times, but there was no answer.
If you rest for a few hours, you'll be fine.
There are a few eggs left in the fridge.
I moved a few months ago.

explain: '두세'와 비슷하게 대략 몇 개를 말할 때 써요. 관형사라서 '두서너 개', '두서너 명'처럼 뒤에 단위 말을 꼭 붙여요. 단독 명사로 쓰는 말은 '두서넛'이에요.
explain_en: Like '두세', it gives a rough small number. It is a determiner, so it must be followed by a counter word, as in '두서너 개' and '두서너 명'. The form that works as a noun on its own is '두서넛'.

examples.en: There are many round rocks by the river.

examples.ko: 그 아저씨는 얼굴이 둥글둥글해서 인상이 좋아요.
examples.en: That man has a round face and gives a good impression.

examples.ko: 우리 형은 성격이 둥글둥글해서 친구가 많아요.
examples.en: My older brother is easygoing, so he has many friends.
Please shape the dough into round balls.
Round fruits are piled on the plate.
The teddy bear is so plump and round that I want to hug it.

explain: '동글동글하다'보다 큰 것이나 포근한 느낌이에요. 모양뿐 아니라 사람의 성격이 모나지 않고 부드러울 때도 써요. 활용은 '둥글둥글해요', '둥글둥글한'이에요.
explain_en: It feels bigger or softer than '동글동글하다'. Besides shape, it also describes a personality that is smooth and not sharp-edged. It conjugates as '둥글둥글해요' and '둥글둥글한'.

examples.ko: 새 부츠가 발에 맞지 않아서 뒤꿈치에 물집이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The new boots didn't fit, so I got a blister on my heel.
My heels crack in winter, so I put on cream.

examples.ko: 아기가 깰까 봐 뒤꿈치를 들고 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked on tiptoe so the baby wouldn't wake up.
The heels of my sneakers are all worn out.
There is a hole in the heel of my sock.
My heel hurt while running, so I went to the hospital.

explain: 몸에서는 '발뒤꿈치'라고 해요. 신발이나 양말의 뒤쪽 부분도 '뒤꿈치'라고 부를 수 있어요. '뒤꿈치를 들다'는 발끝으로 서서 조용히 걷거나 키를 높일 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
explain_en: For the body part the full word is '발뒤꿈치'. The back part of a shoe or sock can also be called '뒤꿈치'. '뒤꿈치를 들다' is used when you stand or walk quietly on your toes or try to look taller.

examples.ko: 이름을 부르자 그가 천천히 뒤돌아서 웃었어요.
examples.en: When I called his name, he slowly turned around and smiled.
Someone called me and I turned around, but nobody was there.
Don't turn around; just look ahead and keep walking.

examples.ko: 선생님이 칠판을 쓰다가 뒤돌아 학생들을 보셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher turned around from writing on the board and looked at the students.

examples.ko: 엄마가 가다가 뒤돌아봐도 아이는 울지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even when Mom looked back while leaving, the child didn't cry.

examples.ko: 저를 보더니 그 사람이 갑자기 뒤돌아요.
examples.en: Seeing me, that person suddenly turns around.

explain: 몸을 돌려 뒤쪽을 향하는 동작이에요. '뒤돌아서다'는 몸 전체를 돌려 서는 느낌이고, '뒤돌아보다'는 뒤를 보는 거예요. '지난날을 뒤돌아보다'처럼 과거를 생각할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes turning your body to face backward. '뒤돌아서다' feels like turning your whole body, and '뒤돌아보다' means looking behind. '지난날을 뒤돌아보다' also uses it for reflecting on the past.

examples.en: If you follow the person ahead, you won't get lost.
The child follows the puppy.
Go ahead. I'll follow right behind you.
We followed the guide and entered the exhibition room.
While following the ambulance, I got stuck at a light.

examples.ko: 친구가 먼저 출발했고 저는 십 분 뒤에 뒤따라갔어요.
examples.en: My friend left first, and I followed ten minutes later.

explain: 말하는 사람에게서 멀어지는 쪽으로 따라갈 때 써요. 반대로 말하는 사람 쪽으로 따라올 때는 '뒤따라오다'를 써요. '쫓아가다'는 잡으려고 따라가는 느낌이 있어서 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when someone follows in a direction away from the speaker. When they follow toward the speaker, use '뒤따라오다'. '쫓아가다' carries a feeling of chasing to catch, so it is different.

examples.ko: 누가 뒤따라오는 것 같아서 돌아보니 제 그림자였어요.
examples.en: I felt someone following me, but when I looked back, it was my shadow.
The puppy keeps following me.

examples.ko: 먼저 가 계세요. 제가 곧 뒤따라올게요.
examples.en: Please go ahead. I'll come along right after you.
The children followed the teacher in a line.

examples.ko: 택시가 우리 차를 계속 뒤따라와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled because a taxi kept following our car.
My friend came along ten minutes later.

explain: 말하는 사람이 있는 쪽으로 누군가 뒤에서 따라올 때 써요. 멀어지는 쪽이면 '뒤따라가다'를 써요. '약속 장소에 먼저 가 있을게요, 뒤따라오세요'처럼 나중에 오라고 말할 때도 좋아요.
explain_en: Use it when someone follows behind toward where the speaker is. If they move away from the speaker, use '뒤따라가다'. It is also handy for telling someone to come later, as in 'I'll be at the meeting spot, please follow after me'.

examples.ko: 뒤뜰에서 닭 몇 마리가 모이를 쪼아 먹고 있어요.
examples.en: A few chickens are pecking at feed in the backyard.
There is a persimmon tree in the backyard of Grandma's house.
On the weekend we grilled meat in the backyard.

examples.ko: 뒤뜰 문을 열면 작은 텃밭이 보여요.
examples.en: If you open the back door, you can see a small vegetable garden.
The kids are playing with a ball in the backyard.
The rain stopped, so I hung the laundry in the backyard.

explain: 집 뒤쪽에 있는 뜰이에요. 짝말은 집 앞쪽의 '앞뜰'이고, 일상에서는 '뒷마당'이라고도 말해요. 단독주택이 아니면 쓸 일이 적은 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the yard at the back of a house, and its counterpart is '앞뜰' at the front. In daily talk people also say '뒷마당'. It comes up less if you don't live in a house with a yard.

examples.en: After the event, I'll take care of the wrap-up.
Please help clean up the milk the child spilled.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일을 벌이기만 하고 뒤처리를 안 해요.
examples.en: That person only starts things and never deals with the aftermath.

examples.ko: 사고 뒤처리 때문에 오늘 늦게 퇴근했어요.
examples.en: I left work late today because of handling the aftermath of an accident.
People who finish things up neatly are easy to trust.
The party wrap-up took longer than I expected.

explain: '뒷정리'는 어질러진 물건을 치우는 거고, '뒤처리'는 일이나 사고가 끝난 뒤 남은 문제를 마무리하는 거예요. 그래서 '사고 뒤처리'처럼 말해요. '뒤처리를 하다', '뒤처리를 맡다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: '뒷정리' is tidying up the mess, while '뒤처리' is wrapping up the remaining problems after a task or accident, as in '사고 뒤처리'. It is commonly used as '뒤처리를 하다' or '뒤처리를 맡다'.

examples.ko: 식사가 끝나면 다 같이 뒷정리를 해요.
examples.en: After the meal, we all clean up together.
I'll do the party cleanup tomorrow.

examples.ko: 마지막까지 남은 사람이 뒷정리를 하고 가야 해요.
examples.en: The person who stays until the end has to tidy up before leaving.
Thank you so much for helping even with the cleanup.

examples.ko: 아이들이 놀고 난 뒤 뒷정리가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Tidying up after the kids have played is tough.

examples.ko: 캠핑이 끝나고 뒷정리에 한 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: After camping, the cleanup took an hour.

explain: 일이나 행사가 끝난 뒤 어질러진 곳을 치우고 정돈하는 걸 말해요. 일 자체를 마무리하는 '뒤처리'와 달리 물건을 치우는 느낌이 강해요. '뒷정리를 하다'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means tidying up the mess after a task or event is over. Unlike '뒤처리', which is about finishing off the matter itself, it mainly feels like putting things away. It is commonly used as '뒷정리를 하다'.

examples.en: We clean up together after dinner.
Who cleans up after the meeting ends?
I'll stay behind, clean up, and then go.
I teach the children to clean up after themselves.
After the event, everyone cleaned up together.
You have to leave the campsite clean.

explain: '정리하다'보다 일이나 모임이 끝난 뒤 남은 것을 치운다는 뜻이 분명해요. '다 같이 뒷정리해요', '뒷정리하고 가요'처럼 쓰고, 명사 '뒷정리'로 '뒷정리를 맡다'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Compared with '정리하다', it clearly means putting away what is left after a task or gathering. It is used as '다 같이 뒷정리해요' or '뒷정리하고 가요', and the noun form works in '뒷정리를 맡다'.

examples.en: I mix the seasoned greens with a little perilla oil.
The nutty smell of perilla oil whets my appetite.

examples.ko: 들기름은 냉장고에 두고 쓰는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to keep perilla oil in the fridge.
I brushed the seaweed with perilla oil and roasted it.
I tried perilla oil noodles for the first time.
I bought a bottle of perilla oil at the market.

explain: 들깨로 짠 기름이에요. 참깨로 짠 '참기름'과 향과 맛이 달라서 요리에서 서로 바꿔 쓰면 맛이 많이 달라져요. 나물, 김, 국수에 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is oil pressed from perilla seeds. It tastes and smells different from '참기름' (sesame oil), so swapping them changes a dish a lot. It is often used on namul, seaweed and noodles.

examples.en: The doorkeeper let the child in.
Please send the patient into the ward.

examples.ko: 방에 신선한 공기를 들여보내려고 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: I opened the window to let fresh air into the room.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아이를 먼저 집 안으로 들여보냈어요.
examples.en: Mom sent the child inside the house first.

examples.ko: 경비원은 신분증이 없는 사람은 안 들여보내요.
examples.en: The guard doesn't let in people without ID.

examples.ko: 시험장 안으로 학생들을 한 명씩 들여보내요.
examples.en: They send the students into the exam hall one by one.

explain: 사람이나 물건, 공기를 밖에서 안으로 보낼 때 써요. 반대말은 '내보내다'예요. 사람에게는 '들여보내 주다'로 말하면 들어가게 허락해 주는 느낌이 나요.
explain_en: Use it for sending people, things or air from outside to inside. The opposite is '내보내다'. With people, '들여보내 주다' sounds like granting permission to enter.

examples.en: Breathe in deeply and then breathe out slowly.
If you breathe in through your nose, you feel calmer.
The doctor told me to breathe in.
I feel good breathing in the clean air.
When you're nervous, try breathing in deeply.
Your belly comes out when you breathe in.

explain: 반대말 '내쉬다'와 짝으로 '숨을 들이쉬고 내쉬세요'라고 말해요. 병원이나 운동할 때 많이 들어요. 공기뿐 아니라 물이나 음료를 마실 때는 '들이마시다'를 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with its opposite '내쉬다' in '숨을 들이쉬고 내쉬세요', which you hear at clinics and in exercise classes. For drinking liquids, use '들이마시다' instead.

examples.ko: 학원 등록비가 한 달에 십만 원이에요.
examples.en: The academy's registration fee is 100,000 won a month.
You have to pay the registration fee when you apply.
I paid the swimming pool registration fee by card.
This year the registration fee went up compared to last year.
The textbook cost is also included in the registration fee.

examples.ko: 이미 낸 등록비를 돌려받을 수 있나요?
examples.en: Can I get back the registration fee I already paid?

explain: 학원, 운동 시설, 동호회 같은 곳에 처음 등록할 때 내는 돈이에요. 대학교에서 내는 돈은 보통 '등록금'이라고 해요. 매달 내는 돈은 '수강료'나 '회비'처럼 따로 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the money you pay when first signing up for places like academies, gyms or clubs. What students pay at a university is usually called '등록금'. Monthly payments are often called '수강료' or '회비'.

examples.en: It's the weekend, so there are lots of hikers on the mountain.

examples.ko: 등산객들이 바위 사이로 난 좁은 길을 지나가요.
examples.en: Hikers pass along a narrow path between the rocks.
A hiker who almost fell off a cliff was rescued.

examples.ko: 정상에서 만난 등산객이 물을 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: A hiker I met at the summit shared some water with me.

examples.ko: 등산객 덕분에 산 아래 식당이 항상 붐벼요.
examples.en: Thanks to the hikers, the restaurants at the foot of the mountain are always crowded.

examples.ko: 시에서 등산객을 위한 쉼터를 새로 만들었어요.
examples.en: The city built a new rest area for hikers.

explain: '-객'은 어떤 곳을 찾아온 손님을 뜻해서 '관광객', '승객'과 같은 짝이에요. 산에 온 사람을 한꺼번에 말할 때 좋고 뉴스에도 자주 나와요. 자기 취미를 말할 때는 '등산을 좋아해요'라고 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-객' marks visitors to a place, like '관광객' and '승객'. This word is good for talking about people on a mountain as a group and shows up in the news. To talk about your own hobby, say '등산을 좋아해요'.

examples.en: This trail is a little hard for beginners.

examples.ko: 등산로 나무마다 길을 알려 주는 표식이 달려 있어요.
examples.en: Every tree along the trail has a marker showing the way.
It rained, so the trail is very slippery.
We decided to meet at the trailhead.

examples.ko: 이 등산로로 올라가면 한 시간쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about an hour if you go up by this trail.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 등산로를 막아 놨어요.
examples.en: A lot of snow fell, so they closed off the trail.

explain: 산을 오르는 길이에요. 가볍게 걷는 길은 '산책로', 둘러 걷는 길은 '둘레길'이라고 해서 쓰임이 달라요. '등산로 입구'처럼 출발하는 곳을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the path used to climb a mountain. A light walking path is a '산책로' and a loop path is a '둘레길', so the uses differ. It is often used for the starting point, as in '등산로 입구'.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 디엔에이 구조를 그려 봤어요.
examples.en: In science class, we drew the structure of DNA.
Parents and children have similar DNA.
Twins have almost identical DNA.
The researchers are analyzing the plant's DNA.
I learned that DNA is like a blueprint of the body.
We confirmed the family relationship through a DNA test.

explain: 글로 쓸 때는 'DNA'라고 영어로 쓰는 일이 많고, 읽을 때는 '디엔에이'라고 해요. '유전자'는 DNA 안의 정보 부분이라 완전히 같은 말은 아니에요. '우리 회사의 DNA'처럼 타고난 특징을 비유로 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: In writing it is often spelled 'DNA' in English letters, and it is read aloud as '디엔에이'. '유전자' (gene) refers to an information part within DNA, so they are not exactly the same word. It is also used figuratively, as in '우리 회사의 DNA', for an inborn trait.

examples.en: With makeup on, you look like a different person.
After coming back from the army, he became a different person.
Don't ask anyone else; ask me.
The person in the photo turned out to be someone else.
These days that friend has brightened up like a different person.
I mistook someone. It was a different person.

explain: '다른 사람'과 비슷한데 '딴'이 붙으면 말투가 더 구어체예요. '딴사람이 되다', '딴사람 같다'는 성격이나 겉모습이 크게 바뀌었다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. '딴생각', '딴판'처럼 '딴-'이 들어간 말이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It is close to '다른 사람', but with '딴' it sounds more colloquial. '딴사람이 되다' and '딴사람 같다' are often used when someone's personality or look has changed a lot. There are more words with '딴-', like '딴생각' and '딴판'.

examples.ko: 회의 때 딴생각을 해서 중요한 내용을 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: I was thinking about something else in the meeting and missed important points.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 딴생각을 하지 말고 공부에 열중하세요.
examples.en: Don't daydream in class; focus on your studies.
I got lost in thought and passed my stop.
It's dangerous if your mind wanders while driving.

examples.ko: 갑자기 딴생각이 들어서 책이 안 읽혀요.
examples.en: Suddenly my mind wandered, and I can't read the book.

examples.ko: 딴생각 없이 한 가지 일만 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: I worked hard on just one thing without any distractions.

explain: 지금 하는 일과 상관없는 다른 생각이에요. 쓸데없는 생각을 뜻하는 '잡생각'과 달리 지금 해야 할 일에서 벗어났다는 점이 핵심이에요. '딴생각을 하다', '딴생각이 들다/나다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It means thoughts unrelated to what you are doing now. Unlike '잡생각' (pointless thoughts), the key point is that your mind has drifted from the task at hand. It goes with '딴생각을 하다' and '딴생각이 들다/나다'.

en: to think of something else; to daydream

examples.en: I was scolded by the teacher for daydreaming during class.
I was thinking about something else earlier, so I didn't hear the question.
When I'm tired, my mind keeps wandering.

examples.ko: 일할 때 딴생각하지 말고 집중해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't let your mind wander and focus while you work.
If you start thinking about other things while studying, time flies.
I was lost in thought on the bus and missed my stop.

explain: '딴생각을 하다'를 줄인 말처럼 쓸 수 있어요. 시선이나 주의를 다른 곳에 두는 '한눈팔다'와 비슷하지만, '딴생각하다'는 머릿속으로 다른 생각을 하는 거예요. 보통 '딴생각하다가 ~했어요'처럼 실수 이유를 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It works like a shortened form of '딴생각을 하다'. It is similar to '한눈팔다' (letting your attention go elsewhere), but '딴생각하다' is about thinking other things in your head. It often appears when explaining a mistake, as in '딴생각하다가 ~했어요'.

examples.en: Beads of sweat formed on my forehead.
The players' sweat dripped onto the floor of the stadium.
I kept running while wiping away the sweat.

examples.ko: 이 금메달은 선수가 흘린 땀방울의 결과예요.
examples.en: This gold medal is the result of the sweat the athlete shed.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 걷기만 해도 땀방울이 흘러요.
examples.en: On hot days, sweat runs down even if I just walk.
Sweat ran all the way down to the tip of my nose.

explain: 그냥 '땀'보다 방울방울 맺힌 모습이 눈에 보이는 말이에요. '땀방울이 맺히다', '땀방울이 떨어지다'처럼 써요. 노력을 비유할 때도 '땀방울'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Compared to plain '땀', it makes you picture the sweat as individual drops. It is used as '땀방울이 맺히다' and '땀방울이 떨어지다'. It is also used figuratively for hard effort.

examples.en: Land prices in this neighborhood go up every year.
Land is expensive, so building a house is hard.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 서울 땅값이 또 올랐다고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said land prices in Seoul rose again.
Land near the station is much more expensive.
I want to sell before land prices fall.
The shop's rent went up too because of land prices.

explain: 집이 아니라 땅 자체의 값이에요. 집을 포함한 값은 '집값'이라고 해서 구별해요. 발음은 [땅깝]이에요.
explain_en: It is the price of the land itself, not of a house. The price including a house is '집값', so the two are distinguished. It is pronounced [땅깝].

examples.en: Try spooning up some of the broth first.

examples.ko: 아이스크림은 작은 숟가락으로 떠먹는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's nice to eat ice cream with a small spoon.

examples.ko: 곰국은 국물부터 떠먹어야 맛을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to taste the broth first to know how the beef soup is.

examples.ko: 밥만 떠먹지 말고 반찬도 같이 드세요.
examples.en: Don't just spoon up rice; eat side dishes with it too.
You eat pudding with a spoon.

examples.ko: 혼자 떠먹기 힘들면 제가 떠 줄게요.
examples.en: If it's hard to scoop and eat it yourself, I'll scoop it for you.

explain: 숟가락이나 국자로 떠서 먹는 방법을 말해요. '퍼먹다'는 더 많이, 마구 퍼서 먹는 느낌이 있어서 달라요. 음식 이름 앞에 '떠먹는 요구르트'처럼 붙이기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes eating by scooping with a spoon or ladle. '퍼먹다' feels more like shoveling in a lot, so it is different. It can also come before a food name, as in '떠먹는 요구르트'.

examples.en: When the rain stopped, the children ran out into the yard.
As soon as he took the call, he ran outside.
The doorbell rang, so I run out to the entrance.
When the door opened, the puppy dashed outside.

examples.ko: 할머니가 손자를 보고 신발도 안 신고 뛰어나가셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma saw her grandson and ran out without even putting on shoes.

examples.ko: 수업이 끝나자 학생들이 교실 밖으로 뛰어나갔어요.
examples.en: When class ended, the students ran out of the classroom.

explain: 밖으로 급하게 달려서 나가는 동작이에요. 말하는 사람 쪽으로 나올 때는 '뛰어나오다'를 써요. '뛰쳐나가다'는 더 급하고 격한 느낌이에요. 높임은 '뛰어나가셨어요'예요.
explain_en: It describes hurrying out by running. When someone comes out toward the speaker, use '뛰어나오다'. '뛰쳐나가다' feels more urgent and intense. The honorific form is '뛰어나가셨어요'.

examples.ko: 뜻있는 사람들이 모여 마을 도서관을 만들었어요.
examples.en: Public-spirited people gathered and built a village library.
I donated money to be used for a worthy cause.

examples.ko: 저도 뜻있는 일을 함께 해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I also want to do something meaningful together.
The school was built with help from well-meaning people.

examples.ko: 뜻있게 시간을 쓰고 싶어서 봉사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: I started volunteering because I wanted to spend my time meaningfully.
Friends with shared goals got together and formed a club.

explain: '뜻있는 사람들'처럼 좋은 뜻을 품은 사람에게 많이 써요. '뜻깊다'는 일이나 날 자체의 의미가 클 때 주로 쓰고, '뜻있다'는 그런 마음을 가진 사람이나 일을 꾸밀 때 자주 나와요. 보통 '뜻있는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
explain_en: It is often used for people with good intentions, as in '뜻있는 사람들'. '뜻깊다' is mainly for an event or day that holds great meaning, while '뜻있다' often describes people or deeds with that spirit. It usually appears as '뜻있는' before a noun.

examples.ko: 사전에서 낱말을 찾으면 뜻풀이 아래에 용례가 함께 나와요.
examples.en: When you look up a word in the dictionary, examples appear below the definition.

examples.ko: 모르는 단어는 뜻풀이를 먼저 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: For words you don't know, read the definition first.
This dictionary is good because its definitions are easy.

examples.ko: 선생님이 어려운 말의 뜻풀이를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher explained the meanings of the difficult words.
I can't get the feeling from the definition alone.
I wrote the definition on the back of the word card.

explain: '뜻'은 단어가 가진 의미 자체이고, '뜻풀이'는 그 의미를 설명해 놓은 글이에요. 그래서 '뜻풀이를 읽다', '뜻풀이를 하다'처럼 말해요. 한자어로는 '정의'라고 해요.
explain_en: '뜻' is the meaning a word has, while '뜻풀이' is the written explanation of that meaning, so you say '뜻풀이를 읽다' or '뜻풀이를 하다'. The Sino-Korean word for it is '정의'.

examples.en: During rush hour, the subway is packed with people.
I go to work early to avoid the rush hour.
I was late for the appointment because of the rush hour.
During the evening rush hour, it's even hard to catch a taxi.

examples.ko: 이 길은 러시아워에 차가 거의 안 움직여요.
examples.en: On this road, cars hardly move during rush hour.
Let's leave once the rush hour is over.

explain: 출근과 퇴근 때 사람과 차가 몰리는 시간이에요. 일상에서는 '출근 시간', '퇴근 시간'이라고 풀어서 많이 말해요. 영어 rush hour처럼 길이 막히는 시간이라는 느낌으로 써요.
explain_en: It is the time when people and cars crowd in around commuting. In daily talk people often say '출근 시간' or '퇴근 시간' instead. It is used just like English 'rush hour', for times when roads and trains are jammed.

examples.en: On a hot day, a cold lemonade is the best.
I ordered a glass of lemonade at the cafe.
Please put more ice in the lemonade.
The children sold lemonade in the yard.
This lemonade is too sweet.
I tried making lemonade from lemons at home.

explain: 레몬즙에 물과 설탕을 넣어 만든 음료예요. 카페 메뉴에서는 '레몬에이드'라고 적혀 있는 것도 자주 볼 수 있어요. 둘 다 비슷한 음료를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is a drink made with lemon juice, water and sugar. On cafe menus you will often see it written as '레몬에이드', and both names refer to a similar drink.

examples.en: There are many old records in Grandpa's room.
When you play a record, a warm sound comes out.

examples.ko: 중고 가게에서 레코드판을 한 장 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a record at a used shop.

examples.ko: 요즘 레코드판을 모으는 젊은 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: These days there are young people who collect records.
Dust has built up on the record, so the sound skips.
I carefully put the needle on the record.

explain: 바늘로 소리를 읽는 둥근 음반이에요. 'LP판'이라고도 하고, CD까지 포함하는 넓은 말은 '음반'이에요. 옛날 물건이라는 느낌이 있어서 추억 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the round disc played with a needle. It is also called 'LP판', and the broader word that includes CDs is '음반'. It carries an old-time feeling and often appears in nostalgic talk.

examples.en: Please write your Korean name in the Roman alphabet.
The name is written in Roman letters on the passport.

examples.ko: 로마자로 쓰면 한국어 발음을 알기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you write it in Roman letters, the Korean pronunciation is easy to see.

examples.ko: 이 간판에는 한글과 로마자가 같이 있어요.
examples.en: This sign has both Hangul and Roman letters.
I'm learning the Romanization rules these days.
The spelling of the Roman-letter name is wrong.

explain: 영어뿐 아니라 프랑스어, 스페인어 같은 여러 언어가 쓰는 라틴 문자를 가리켜요. 한글을 로마자로 옮겨 적는 걸 '로마자 표기'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '알파벳'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the Latin script used not only by English but by French, Spanish and many other languages. Writing Hangul in these letters is called '로마자 표기'. In daily talk people also say '알파벳'.
